Simulate synthetic BDHS-like recode data

Source: R/simulate.R
bdhs_simulate.Rd

Generates fake data with the structure of a BDHS recode file: the same variable names, codes, value labels, identifiers and complex survey design variables (clusters, strata, weights, all-women factors) as the real files. Every value is randomly generated, so the output can be shared freely. It powers the package examples, tests and vignettes, and lets you write and test analysis code before you have DHS access.

Usage

bdhs_simulate(
  survey = 2022,
  recode = c("IR", "KR", "BR", "HR", "PR"),
  n_clusters = 40,
  households = 15,
  seed = 1
)

Arguments

survey

A survey reference understood by bdhs_survey_id(). Only the standard DHS rounds are supported.

recode

One of "IR" (women), "KR" (children under 5), "BR" (births), "HR" (households) or "PR" (household members).

n_clusters

Number of clusters (primary sampling units) to simulate.

households

Households per cluster.

seed

Random seed. The same seed always gives the same population; the global random number generator state is left untouched.

Value

A tibble with lower-case DHS variable names and haven-labelled columns, carrying the attributes bdhs_survey_id, bdhs_recode and bdhs_simulated = TRUE.

Details

All recodes simulated with the same survey and seed describe the same synthetic population, so they can be linked with bdhs_merge() exactly like real files: women in "IR" are household members in "PR", children in "KR" are births in "BR", and so on.

The data are structurally faithful: region codes follow the division layout of the requested round (5 divisions in 1993-94, 8 from 2017-18), and the core variables use DHS-7 coding. They are not statistically faithful, and round-specific coding changes in less common variables are not reproduced. Never use simulated data for substantive conclusions.

Examples

ir <- bdhs_simulate(2022, "IR")
ir[1:5, c("caseid", "v001", "v005", "v022", "v024", "v025", "v012", "v313")]
#> # A tibble: 5 × 8
#>   caseid             v001   v005 v022              v024    v025     v012 v313   
#>   <chr>             <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl+lbl>         <dbl+l> <dbl+l> <dbl> <dbl+l>
#> 1 "       1   2  2"     1 744251 1 [barishal urba… 1 [bar… 1 [urb…    22 3 [mod…
#> 2 "       1   3  2"     1 744251 1 [barishal urba… 1 [bar… 1 [urb…    20 0 [no …
#> 3 "       1   4  2"     1 744251 1 [barishal urba… 1 [bar… 1 [urb…    32 0 [no …
#> 4 "       1   5  2"     1 744251 1 [barishal urba… 1 [bar… 1 [urb…    19 0 [no …
#> 5 "       1   6  2"     1 744251 1 [barishal urba… 1 [bar… 1 [urb…    49 3 [mod…

# The same synthetic population in household-member form
pr <- bdhs_simulate(2022, "PR")
nrow(pr)
#> [1] 3006
